Sorry, but that article is poorly written and just plain stupid. Honestly, the only "hate" I've seen thrown around regarding an OS is from Linux users who pretty much shit on anything other than Linux. All you have to do is read Voat to see how unhinged Linux users have become. Instead of fixating so much on Microsoft or Windows 10, why don't you guys work at getting rid of Terminal in Linux so more people will be comfortable using it?

You want Linix developers to remove the Terminal, just so people feel more comfortable using the Operating System?

No, just no. The terminal is an essential tool for maintaining a linux operating system. It is not hard to understand it and how to use it properly. If people are that scared of a great black window with blinking white cursor, then they can use a distro like Ubuntu which tries to limit your exposure to it as much as possible.

The closest Windows comparison I can think of, would be demanding Microsoft remove Powershell from their latest OS, because those who do not know how to use it are intimidated by it. Complete nonsense. Punish the power users by removing a useful tool so that the casual users feel better. No thanks.

My point regarding Terminal is that it is absolutely required to do BASIC things in Linux. Almost all troubleshooting an issue involves issuing Terminal commands.

I began programming in the 70s and like everyone else, had to use DOS extensively for years. I still love DOS and often drop to a command-line interface to do basic stuff so I appreciate what you write about denying power-users a great tool. However no modern operating system requires normal users to learn a command-line interface at this point. It has been decades since users were compelled to learn these type of commands. Nobody outside of enthusiasts or "powerusers" has any desire to memorize an arcane set of commands that give you little to no feedback on whether the desired result was achieved.

Unfortunately Linux refuses to phase out Terminal which is extremely off-putting to normal folks who might be interested. Requiring normal folks to learn an arcane command-line interface to do basic tasks makes the barrier to entry far too high for most folks, yet Linux advocates continue to bemoan the fact that more people don't switch. I'd speculate this is one of the drawbacks with OS software--since it is developed by folks who are technically savvy, they are often blind (or indifferent) to the needs of those who are not. Regardless, Linux will never be a mainstream OS as long as it requires users to issue Terminal commands to perform routine functions.
Do you have an example of a basic task that a casual user would want to carry out, which requires the terminal, that does not have a GUI front end?

Sure. I've consistently had difficulty with getting alsa drivers to work. This has been an issue across multiple systems over multiple years that I've personally dealt with. The only way to troubleshoot it and get it resolved is to spend time in Terminal. That's a lot of trouble just to get sound working in certain games.

I've brought this issue of Terminal up on other threads and I very often get other folks agreeing with me. Linux advocates, unfortunately, don't like to hear any critical feedback and often downvoat. I'm not even bashing Linux (I've used Linux since the mid-90s). I'm just stating the facts--and anybody who uses Linux KNOWS that you do have to use Terminal...you probably just don't think about it since you've learned it. But that doesn't change the fact that it is extremely antiquated and is keeping Linux from being more widely adopted.

Well that sucks.

Though I will say, if you are going to have issues with Linux, it will most probably be a hardware/driver issue.

Though I fail to see how removing the terminal would improve matters in that regard, especially when you consider removing the terminal would require a complete redesign of how the Linux kernel operates and how the user interacts with the Kernel.

Devs time would probably be better spent improving GUI front-end tools and creating more reliable open source drivers for hardware.

What do you envision replacing the terminal/console?

I don't develop for Linux so I'm not a good person to ask about a possible technical alternative. But look at how Mac OS and Windows handles such tasks--there is absolutely no requirement to drop to a terminal interface. And that's really the crux of the matter--giving the end-user an experience that they can ease into without creating a barrier that they're unwilling and/or unable to overcome. None of the major consumer OS's (Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android) requires users to use a command-line, so if Linux users insist on this feature just accept that the OS will never attract a significant number of folks. Without trying to sound sarcastic (I'm being sincere) it's 2016--Microsoft moved away from DOS configurations in Windows 95--over 20 years ago. There are literally generations of computer users who have no experience with such things. If you participate at XDA you'll find scores of people who have no idea how to issue ADB commands or use Terminal--and those are folks who are at least motivated to TRY to do so...the vast majority of people are dependent on devs who create 1-click tools for them.

My comments regarding Linux & Terminal are not meant to denigrate the OS, but regardless of how I articulate this simple, fact-based feedback I almost always get attacked because Linux users typically push-back on ANY notion that the OS is not superior. Linux is great, but it will never be widely adopted by end-users until it changes some fundamental elements. Unfortunately the attitude of your typical Linux enthusiast is "let them learn Terminal" and not "yeah, that needs to be made more user-friendly."
